baslik: The Steamship Wrecked Within Sight of Shore
sonuc: ran onto a reef off Vancouver Island
tetik: a navigation error by dead reckoning in fog
mekanizma: grounding after overshooting the strait entrance, followed by failed lifeboat launches in heavy surf
ders: a lighthouse and a lifesaving trail were built along that coast
yanilgi: Most victims didn't die in the impact. They died over the following days as rescue failed.
tartisma: Rescue ships arrived but couldn't reach the wreck. How close is too far?
basliklar: Why the SS Valencia Was Wrecked
The Shipwreck Rescuers Couldn't Reach
sahneler: In fog, the steamship Valencia ran onto a reef off Vancouver Island.
Over the next days, most of the people aboard were killed.
The crew had estimated position without landmarks.
They overshot the entrance to the strait.
The ship struck rocks below steep cliffs.
Lifeboats capsized in the heavy surf.
Rescue ships came but couldn't get close.
A lighthouse and a lifesaving trail were built on that coast.

commons: SS City of Rio de Janeiro
baslik: The Liner That Sank at the Golden Gate in Fog
ad: the SS City of Rio de Janeiro
sonuc: struck rocks at the entrance to San Francisco Bay
tetik: entering the Golden Gate in thick fog
mekanizma: grounding in fog followed by rapid flooding and a chaotic evacuation
ders: the wreck spurred improvements to navigation aids at the Golden Gate
yanilgi: The ship sank within sight of the city. Language barriers among the crew slowed the evacuation.
tartisma: The pilot chose to proceed in fog. When should a ship wait?
basliklar: Why the City of Rio de Janeiro Sank
The Wreck at the Golden Gate
hook: It sank at the Golden Gate
sahneler: A passenger liner struck rocks at the entrance to San Francisco Bay.
It sank in minutes, killing one hundred twenty eight people.
Thick fog covered the Golden Gate.
The pilot decided to proceed.
The ship hit submerged rocks.
Water flooded in quickly.
The crew struggled to organize the evacuation.
Navigation aids at the Golden Gate were improved afterward.

baslik: The Iron Ship Whose Compasses Lied
sonuc: ran aground on its maiden voyage
tetik: compasses deflected by the ship's own iron hull
mekanizma: magnetic deviation from an iron hull that the compasses were not corrected for
ders: the case pushed research into correcting compasses on iron ships
yanilgi: The crew followed their compasses. The compasses were pulled off by the iron hull itself.
tartisma: New materials brought a hidden side effect. How do you find problems nobody has seen yet?
basliklar: Why the RMS Tayleur Was Wrecked
The Compasses Pulled Off Course by Iron
soru: How do you find unseen risks?
sahneler: On its maiden voyage, the iron clipper Tayleur ran aground off Ireland.
It struck rocks on Lambay Island, and hundreds were killed.
The crew had followed their compasses.
But the ship's iron hull disturbed them.
The compasses hadn't been properly corrected.
In poor visibility, the error went unnoticed.
The ship headed straight for the island.
It pushed research into correcting compasses on iron ships.

baslik: A Blob of Paint Sank a New Submarine
tetik: a torpedo tube opened while its outer door was open
mekanizma: a test cock blocked by paint, hiding that the outer bow cap was open
ders: torpedo tube interlocks and test procedures were changed
yanilgi: The crew checked whether the tube was flooded. The check failed because paint blocked the test hole.
tartisma: Part of the stern stayed above water for hours. Why couldn't more men be saved?
basliklar: Why HMS Thetis Sank
The Paint That Hid an Open Door
sahneler: A brand-new British submarine sank during its first dive.
Within hours, ninety nine men were dead.
A torpedo tube was opened from inside.
Its outer door was already open to the sea.
A small test hole should have shown water in the tube.
It had been blocked by paint.
The sea flooded the bow, and only four men escaped.
Torpedo tube interlocks and tests were changed.

baslik: The First Submarine Rescue in History
sonuc: flooded and sank on a test dive
tetik: a main induction valve failing to close
mekanizma: failure of the main engine air induction valve flooding the aft compartments
ders: the McCann rescue chamber proved submarine rescue was possible
yanilgi: Not everyone was lost. A new rescue chamber brought survivors up from the seabed.
tartisma: The indicator showed the valve closed. How much should crews trust indicator lights?
basliklar: Why USS Squalus Sank
The First Submarine Rescue
sahneler: During a test dive, the submarine Squalus suddenly flooded.
It sank to the seabed, and twenty six men were killed.
A main air induction valve had failed to close.
Seawater poured into the rear compartments.
Thirty three men survived in the forward part.
Rescuers lowered a new diving bell called the McCann chamber.
It brought all thirty three to the surface.
It was the first successful submarine rescue.

baslik: The Ferry That Capsized at the Mouth of Wellington Harbour
sonuc: struck a reef and capsized in a storm
tetik: a cyclone driving the ferry onto Barrett Reef
mekanizma: grounding in extreme winds, then flooding and capsize inside the harbour
ders: the disaster shaped New Zealand's approach to ferry safety and rescue
yanilgi: The ship capsized inside the harbour, close to shore. The storm made rescue extremely hard.
tartisma: The order to abandon ship came late in the day. How do you time an evacuation in a storm?
basliklar: Why the Wahine Capsized
The Ferry Lost Inside Wellington Harbour
sahneler: In a violent storm, the ferry Wahine struck a reef at Wellington's harbour entrance.
Hours later it capsized, and dozens of people were killed.
A tropical cyclone collided with a southerly storm.
Winds pushed the ship onto Barrett Reef.
Damaged and flooding, it drifted into the harbour.
The order to abandon ship came in the afternoon.
Many were swept to the far shore by wind and waves.
The disaster shaped New Zealand's ferry safety and rescue planning.

baslik: A Shortcut Put a Container Ship on a Charted Reef
sonuc: ran aground on a reef off New Zealand
tetik: a course shortcut to reach port on time
mekanizma: grounding on a charted reef after altering course without proper navigation checks
ders: New Zealand strengthened maritime pollution response and navigation oversight
yanilgi: The reef was on the charts. The ship's new course ran straight across it.
tartisma: The captain and officer were jailed. Should navigation errors be crimes?
basliklar: Why the MV Rena Ran Aground
The Shortcut Across a Charted Reef
hook: The reef was on the chart
sahneler: A container ship ran aground on a reef off New Zealand.
Within days, oil and containers spilled into the sea as the hull cracked.
The ship was running late.
The crew shortened the route to reach port on time.
The new course crossed a reef marked on the chart.
It hit the reef at speed in the early morning.
Oil fouled beaches along the Bay of Plenty.
Pollution response and navigation oversight were strengthened.

baslik: The Anchor Handler Pulled Over by Its Own Chain
sonuc: capsized while handling a rig's anchor
tetik: a heavy anchor chain pulling the ship sideways
mekanizma: loss of stability from chain tension at a steep angle during anchor handling
ders: an inquiry questioned whether the vessel and crew were ready for deep-water anchor handling
yanilgi: The sea wasn't the main problem. The chain's sideways pull overcame the ship's stability.
tartisma: The vessel was new and the crew relatively inexperienced with it. How much experience should a hazardous job require?
basliklar: Why the Bourbon Dolphin Capsized
The Chain That Pulled a Ship Over
hook: Its own chain pulled it over
sahneler: An anchor handling vessel capsized in the North Sea.
It rolled over while working, and members of its crew were killed.
It was moving a heavy anchor chain for an oil rig.
The chain drifted off to the side.
Its enormous weight pulled the ship sideways.
The ship heeled beyond recovery.
Its new captain had only ninety minutes to take over.
An inquiry questioned whether ship and crew were ready for such deep water.

baslik: The Tornado That Knocked Down a Historic Viaduct
sonuc: was knocked down by a tornado
tetik: tornado winds on towers with corroded anchor bolts
mekanizma: failure of rusted anchor bolts letting towers topple under wind load
ders: the ruins were kept as a skywalk and monument to the failure
yanilgi: The tornado wasn't extremely strong. The towers' anchor bolts had rusted badly.
tartisma: The bridge was already closed for repairs. How do you prioritize fixing ageing landmarks?
basliklar: Why the Kinzua Bridge Collapsed
The Rusted Bolts Under a Historic Viaduct
sahneler: A tornado swept across a historic railway viaduct in Pennsylvania.
Within seconds, its towers were ripped from their bases and fell.
The viaduct was already closed for repairs.
Its anchor bolts had badly corroded.
They could no longer hold the towers to their footings.
The wind knocked them over.
Nobody was on it.
The remaining span became a skywalk above the wreckage.

baslik: A Barge Knocked Out a Causeway and Cars Drove Into the Gap
sonuc: lost spans when a barge hit a pier
tetik: a tow drifting out of the channel at night
mekanizma: barge impact on an unprotected pier dropping spans
ders: the causeway got a gap-detection warning system
yanilgi: Most deaths happened after the collapse, as drivers who couldn't see the gap drove into it.
tartisma: Nothing warned drivers of the missing section. How should a bridge warn traffic it's gone?
basliklar: Why the Queen Isabella Causeway Collapsed
The Gap Drivers Couldn't See
sahneler: At night, a tow pushing barges hit a pier of a Texas causeway.
Spans fell into the water, and eight people were killed.
The tow had drifted out of the channel.
The pier had no protection against a barge.
In the dark, drivers couldn't see the gap.
Several vehicles drove straight into it.
Fishermen rescued survivors from the water.
The causeway now has a warning system for missing spans.

baslik: Hurricane Waves Lifted a Bridge Off Its Piers
sonuc: had dozens of spans knocked off their piers
tetik: storm surge and waves from Hurricane Katrina
mekanizma: surge raising water to the deck while waves lifted spans that were not anchored against uplift
ders: the replacement bridge was built higher above the water
yanilgi: The bridge wasn't pushed sideways by wind. Water lifted the spans off their supports.
tartisma: The spans were held mainly by their own weight. Should bridges near coasts be anchored against uplift?
basliklar: How Hurricane Katrina Lifted the I-10 Twin Span
The Bridge Spans That Floated Away
sahneler: Hurricane Katrina knocked dozens of spans off a bridge near New Orleans.
Within hours, the interstate link across Lake Pontchartrain was cut.
Storm surge raised the water up to the bridge deck.
Waves pushed up from beneath.
The spans were held mostly by their own weight.
They were lifted and dropped off their piers.
Air trapped under the deck added buoyancy.
The replacement bridge was built much higher.

baslik: A Cart of Hay Started a Deadly Mine Fire
sonuc: caught fire, trapping hundreds of miners
tetik: hay bales ignited by a kerosene torch
mekanizma: fire in a mine shaft fed by hay and timber, with fans spreading smoke
ders: Illinois passed mine safety and workers' compensation laws
zincir: HAY BALES ON A MINE CART
yanilgi: Some miners survived for eight days behind a wall they built themselves.
tartisma: Sealing the shaft stopped the fire but trapped the miners. Was it the right call?
basliklar: Why the Cherry Mine Fire Was So Deadly
The Hay Bales That Started a Mine Fire
sahneler: Fire broke out deep in an Illinois coal mine.
It trapped hundreds underground, and two hundred fifty nine men and boys died.
Bales of hay for the mine's mules were on a cart.
A kerosene torch dripped onto them and they caught fire.
Flames spread to the mine's timbers.
The shaft was sealed to smother the fire.
A group of miners survived for eight days behind a wall they built.
Illinois passed mine safety and compensation laws afterward.

baslik: The Supermarket Roof That Collapsed Under a Garden
sonuc: had its roof collapse onto shoppers
tetik: a rooftop garden and heavy soil being added
mekanizma: design and construction errors in roof trusses overloaded by a rooftop garden
ders: Latvia overhauled building inspection and construction oversight
yanilgi: A fire alarm sounded before the collapse. Shoppers weren't evacuated.
tartisma: The alarm was treated as a false alarm. How do you keep alarms from being ignored?
basliklar: Why the Zolitūde Supermarket Roof Collapsed
The Rooftop Garden That Brought Down a Roof
sahneler: The roof of a Riga supermarket collapsed on a busy evening.
Shoppers and rescuers were crushed, and fifty four people died.
A rooftop garden was being built above the store.
Heavy soil had been placed on the roof.
The roof's steel trusses had design and construction flaws.
A fire alarm sounded, but shoppers weren't evacuated.
More of the roof fell as rescuers worked.
Latvia overhauled building inspection afterward.

baslik: The Cheaply Built Dam That Swept Away Four Villages
sonuc: failed and flooded four Massachusetts villages
tetik: leakage through a poorly built embankment
mekanizma: failure of an earthen dam built with cost-cutting changes to its core wall
ders: Massachusetts passed laws requiring inspection of dams
yanilgi: The dam wasn't old. It had been built cheaply only about a decade before.
tartisma: Mill owners built it to power their factories. Who is responsible for a private dam's failure?
basliklar: Why the Mill River Dam Failed
The Cheap Dam That Flooded Four Villages
soru: Who pays when a private dam fails?
sahneler: A dam above Williamsburg, Massachusetts, burst one morning.
Floodwater swept through four villages, and one hundred thirty nine people died.
The dam had been built about a decade earlier.
It powered local mills.
Its design had been changed to save money.
Seepage weakened the embankment until it slid away.
A dam keeper rode to warn people downstream.
Massachusetts then passed laws requiring dam inspections.

baslik: A Crosswind Gust Pushed a Jet Off the Runway
sonuc: veered off the runway and caught fire at Denver
tetik: a strong crosswind gust during take-off
mekanizma: loss of directional control in a gusting crosswind beyond what the crew expected
ders: crosswind training and wind information at Denver were improved
yanilgi: The wind reported to the crew was lower than the gusts on the runway.
tartisma: Everyone survived because the evacuation worked. How much credit goes to cabin crew?
basliklar: Why Continental Flight 1404 Left the Runway
The Gust That Pushed a Jet Sideways
sahneler: During take-off at Denver, a Boeing 737 veered off the runway.
It crossed a ravine and caught fire, but everyone survived.
Strong, gusty winds were blowing across the runway.
The wind reported to the crew was lower than the gusts.
A gust pushed the jet sideways during the take-off roll.
The captain couldn't keep it on the centreline.
Passengers evacuated before the fire spread.
Crosswind training and wind reporting were improved.
